Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import unittest

from provenance_api.app import application, reset_state

DIGEST_A = "a" * 64
DIGEST_B = "b" * 64
DIGEST_C = "c" * 64

PATH = "/digest-usage"


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
    content_length: int | str | None = None,
    omit_content_length: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "QUERY_STRING": query_string if query_string is not None else "",
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    if not omit_content_length:
        environ["CONTENT_LENGTH"] = (
            str(len(payload)) if content_length is None else str(content_length)
        )
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def start_response(status: str, headers: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        captured["status"] = status
        captured["headers"] = headers

    chunks = application(environ, start_response)
    return str(captured["status"]), list(captured["headers"]), b"".join(chunks)


def call_json(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    **kwargs: object,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], object]:
    status, headers, raw = call(method, path, body, **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return status, headers, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))


class DigestUsageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _create(
        self,
        name: str,
        digest: str,
        *,
        category: str = "code",
    ) -> str:
        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",
            {"name": name, "category": category, "digest": digest},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        return str(body["id"])  # type: ignore[index]

    def _usage(self, **kwargs: object):
        return call("GET", PATH, **kwargs)

    def _usage_json(self, body: object = None, **kwargs: object):
        status, headers, parsed = call_json("GET", PATH, body, **kwargs)
        return status, headers, parsed

    # --- Empty registry ------------------------------------------------------

    def test_empty_registry_is_empty_array_success(self) -> None:
        status, headers, raw = self._usage()
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(
            headers[0], ("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        )
        self.assertEqual(raw, b"[]\n")

    # --- Entry shape and ordering -------------------------------------------

    def test_one_entry_per_digest_in_first_appearance_order(self) -> None:
        # b first, then a twice: entries must follow [b, a], never sorted.
        b1 = self._create("b-one", DIGEST_B)
        a1 = self._create("a-one", DIGEST_A)
        a2 = self._create("a-two", DIGEST_A, category="model")

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(  # type: ignore[index]
            [entry["digest"] for entry in body], [DIGEST_B, DIGEST_A]
        )
        entries = {entry["digest"]: entry for entry in body}  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_B]["resources"], [b1])
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_A]["resources"], [a1, a2])
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_A]["resource_count"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_A]["names"], ["a-one", "a-two"])

    def test_entry_key_order_is_fixed(self) -> None:
        self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        for entry in body:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            self.assertEqual(
                list(entry),
                ["digest", "resources", "resource_count", "names"],
            )

    def test_digest_is_echoed_as_normalized_lowercase(self) -> None:
        self._create("upper", "A" * 64)
        self._create("mixed", "Ab" + "0" * 62)
        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(  # type: ignore[index]
            [entry["digest"] for entry in body],
            [DIGEST_A, "ab" + "0" * 62],
        )

    def test_uppercase_digest_merges_with_lowercase_group(self) -> None:
        lower = self._create("lower", DIGEST_A)
        upper = self._create("upper", "A" * 64, category="model")
        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(len(body), 1)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        entry = body[0]  # type: ignore[index]
        self.assertEqual(entry["digest"], DIGEST_A)
        self.assertEqual(entry["resources"], [lower, upper])
        self.assertEqual(entry["resource_count"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(entry["names"], ["lower", "upper"])

    def test_names_deduplicated_but_case_and_whitespace_preserved(self) -> None:
        # Same (name, digest) pair under two categories yields two resources;
        # the name must appear in ``names`` only once.
        one = self._create("Model", DIGEST_A)
        two = self._create("Model", DIGEST_A, category="model")
        # Case and surrounding whitespace are significant.
        three = self._create("model", DIGEST_A, category="dataset")
        four = self._create(" Model ", DIGEST_A, category="artifact")

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        entry = body[0]  # type: ignore[index]
        self.assertEqual(entry["resources"], [one, two, three, four])
        self.assertEqual(entry["resource_count"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(entry["names"], ["Model", "model", " Model "])

    def test_resource_count_matches_resources_length(self) -> None:
        self._create("a1", DIGEST_A)
        self._create("a2", DIGEST_A, category="model")
        self._create("same", DIGEST_A, category="dataset")
        self._create("same", DIGEST_A, category="artifact")
        self._create("b1", DIGEST_B)
        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        for entry in body:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            self.assertEqual(
                entry["resource_count"], len(entry["resources"])
            )

    # --- Recomputation and read-only behavior --------------------------------

    def test_recompute_after_registration(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual([entry["digest"] for entry in body], [DIGEST_A])  # type: ignore[index]

        # A resource of an existing digest appends to that group.
        a2 = self._create("a2", DIGEST_A, category="model")
        # A new digest gets a fresh trailing entry.
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(  # type: ignore[index]
            [entry["digest"] for entry in body], [DIGEST_A, DIGEST_B]
        )
        entries = {entry["digest"]: entry for entry in body}  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_A]["resources"], [a, a2])
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_A]["names"], ["a", "a2"])
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_B]["resources"], [b])

    def test_entry_disappears_when_digest_loses_every_resource(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)

        status, _h, _raw = call("DELETE", f"/resources/{b}")
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(  # type: ignore[index]
            [entry["digest"] for entry in body], [DIGEST_A, DIGEST_C]
        )
        self.assertNotIn(DIGEST_B, [entry["digest"] for entry in body])
        entries = {entry["digest"]: entry for entry in body}  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_A]["resources"], [a])
        self.assertEqual(entries[DIGEST_C]["resources"], [c])

    def test_delete_first_resource_redetermines_entry_order(self) -> None:
        # a holds positions 1 and 3, b position 2. Deleting the first a
        # resource redetermines first-appearance order from the remaining
        # registry: b is now earlier than the surviving a, so the b entry
        # moves to the front and no stale slot is left behind.
        first_a = self._create("a-one", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b-one", DIGEST_B)
        second_a = self._create("a-two", DIGEST_A, category="model")

        status, _h, _raw = call("DELETE", f"/resources/{first_a}")
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(  # type: ignore[index]
            [entry["digest"] for entry in body], [DIGEST_B, DIGEST_A]
        )
        self.assertEqual(body[0]["resources"], [b])  # type: ignore[index]
        entry_a = body[1]  # type: ignore[index]
        self.assertEqual(entry_a["resources"], [second_a])
        self.assertEqual(entry_a["resource_count"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(entry_a["names"], ["a-two"])

    def test_delete_first_group_shifts_remaining_entries_forward(self) -> None:
        first = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)

        status, _h, _raw = call("DELETE", f"/resources/{first}")
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(  # type: ignore[index]
            [entry["digest"] for entry in body], [DIGEST_B, DIGEST_C]
        )
        self.assertEqual(body[0]["resources"], [b])  # type: ignore[index]
        self.assertEqual(body[1]["resources"], [c])  # type: ignore[index]

    def test_name_disappears_with_its_last_resource(self) -> None:
        a1 = self._create("shared", DIGEST_A)
        a2 = self._create("other", DIGEST_A, category="model")

        status, _h, _raw = call("DELETE", f"/resources/{a1}")
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(body[0]["names"], ["other"])  # type: ignore[index]
        self.assertEqual(body[0]["resources"], [a2])  # type: ignore[index]

    def test_view_is_read_only(self) -> None:
        self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        self._create("b", DIGEST_B, category="model")

        self._usage()
        self._usage()

        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(len(listing["resources"]), 2)  # type: ignore[index]
        _s, _h, body = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(len(body), 2)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    def test_existing_resource_entry_points_keep_their_behavior(self) -> None:
        # Registration query and list pagination are untouched by the view.
        resource = self._create("a", DIGEST_A, category="artifact")
        _s, _h, item = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{resource}")
        self.assertEqual(item["digest"], DIGEST_A)  # type: ignore[index]
        _s, _h, page = call_json(
            "GET", "/resources", query_string="limit=1"
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(page["resources"]), 1)  # type: ignore[index]
        self.assertEqual(page["resources"][0]["id"], resource)  # type: ignore[index]

    # --- Response body -------------------------------------------------------

    def test_body_is_compact_json_with_single_trailing_newline(self) -> None:
        rid = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        _s, _h, raw = self._usage()
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(raw.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        self.assertEqual(
            raw,
            b'[{"digest":"'
            + DIGEST_A.encode("ascii")
            + b'","resources":["'
            + rid.encode("ascii")
            + b'"],"resource_count":1,"names":["a"]}]\n',
        )

    def test_no_persistence_files_created(self) -> None:
        import pathlib

        root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
        before = {
            str(p.relative_to(root))
            for p in root.rglob("*")
            if ".git" not in p.parts and p.is_file()
        }
        self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        self._usage()
        after = {
            str(p.relative_to(root))
            for p in root.rglob("*")
            if ".git" not in p.parts and p.is_file()
        }
        self.assertEqual(before, after)

    # --- Validation ----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_query_parameters_are_bad_request(self) -> None:
        self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        for query_string in (
            "bogus=1",
            "=",
            "x=&y=2",
            "x=1&x=2",
            "digest=" + DIGEST_A,
            "foo",
        ):
            with self.subTest(query_string=query_string):
                status, _h, body = call_json(
                    "GET", PATH, query_string=query_string
                )
                self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
                self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")  # type: ignore[index]

    def test_declared_non_empty_body_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        status, _h, body = call_json("GET", PATH, b"{}")
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")  # type: ignore[index]

        # The rejected request changed nothing.
        _s, _h, usage = self._usage_json()
        self.assertEqual(len(usage), 1)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    def test_malformed_content_length_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        status, _h, body = call_json("GET", PATH, content_length="abc")
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")  # type: ignore[index]

    def test_bad_request_does_not_read_business_data(self) -> None:
        self._create("a", DIGEST_A)

    def test_omitted_length_header_is_accepted(self) -> None:

69	def build_resource_fields(
70	    payload: object,
71	) -> tuple[str, str, str, str | None]:
72	    """Validate a decoded JSON payload and return normalized field values."""
73	
74	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
75	        raise ResourceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
76	
77	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
78	    if unknown_fields:
79	        raise ResourceValidationError(
80	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
81	        )
82	
83	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
84	        if field not in payload:
85	            raise ResourceValidationError(
86	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
87	            )
88	
89	    name = _require_non_empty_string(payload["name"], "Name")
90	
91	    category_raw = payload["category"]
92	    if not isinstance(category_raw, str):
93	        raise ResourceValidationError("Category must be a string.")
94	    category = category_raw.lower()
95	    if category not in _CATEGORY_VALUES:
96	        allowed = ", ".join(CATEGORIES)
97	        raise ResourceValidationError(
98	            f"Category must be one of: {allowed} (case-insensitive)."
99	        )
100	
101	    digest_raw = payload["digest"]
102	    if not isinstance(digest_raw, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(
103	        digest_raw
104	    ) is None:
105	        raise ResourceValidationError(
106	            "Digest must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
107	        )
108	    # Hexadecimal digests are case-insensitive; store them canonically.
109	    digest = digest_raw.lower()
110	
111	    source: str | None = None
112	    if "source" in payload:
113	        source = _require_non_empty_string(payload["source"], "Source")
114	
115	    return name, category, digest, source

118	def build_dependency_batch_fields(
119	    payload: object, *, reject_duplicates: bool = False
120	) -> list[str]:
121	    """Validate a decoded dependency batch payload, returning the id list.
122	
123	    The top level must be a JSON object carrying exactly one field,
124	    ``dependencies``: a non-empty array of at most
125	    :data:`MAX_DEPENDENCY_BATCH_SIZE` non-empty strings, none containing a
126	    path separator (``/`` or ``\\``). The ids are returned in their
127	    submitted order.
128	
129	    When ``reject_duplicates`` is set (the batch-removal path), an id
130	    repeated inside the array is rejected here like every other shape
131	    error, so the request fails before any business data is read. The
132	    batch-registration path leaves the flag clear: its repeat check is
133	    ordered after self loops (but before existing-edge and cycle checks)
134	    in :meth:`ResourceStore.add_dependencies` so that, e.g., a
135	    self-referential repeated entry reports the cycle rather than the
136	    repeat. Existence and graph conflicts are likewise checked later so
137	    their error codes keep precedence.
138	    """
139	
140	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
141	        raise ResourceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
142	
143	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - {"dependencies"}
144	    if unknown_fields:
145	        raise ResourceValidationError(
146	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
147	        )
148	    if "dependencies" not in payload:
149	        raise ResourceValidationError(
150	            "Missing required field: 'dependencies'."
151	        )
152	
153	    items = payload["dependencies"]
154	    if not isinstance(items, list):
155	        raise ResourceValidationError(
156	            "Field 'dependencies' must be an array."
157	        )
158	    if not items:
159	        raise ResourceValidationError(
160	            "Field 'dependencies' must not be empty."
161	        )
162	    if len(items) > MAX_DEPENDENCY_BATCH_SIZE:
163	        raise ResourceValidationError(
164	            f"Field 'dependencies' must not exceed "
165	            f"{MAX_DEPENDENCY_BATCH_SIZE} entries."
166	        )
167	
168	    dependency_ids: list[str] = []
169	    seen: set[str] = set()
170	    for position, item in enumerate(items):
171	        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item:
172	            raise ResourceValidationError(
173	                f"Dependency at index {position} must be a non-empty string."
174	            )
175	        if "/" in item or "\\" in item:
176	            raise ResourceValidationError(
177	                f"Dependency at index {position} must not contain path "
178	                "separators."
179	            )
180	        if reject_duplicates and item in seen:
181	            raise ResourceValidationError(
182	                "A dependency must not be listed more than once in the "
183	                "same batch."
184	            )
185	        seen.add(item)
186	        dependency_ids.append(item)
187	
188	    return dependency_ids

191	class ResourceStore:
192	    """Process-local, insertion-ordered resource storage."""
193	
194	    def __init__(self) -> None:
195	        self._resources: list[Resource] = []
196	        self._by_id: dict[str, Resource] = {}
197	        self._key_to_id: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] = {}
198	        # resource id -> ids it directly depends on, and the reverse view.
199	        # Insertion-ordered dicts stand in for ordered sets: membership stays
200	        # O(1) while iteration remembers the order in which each relation was
201	        # established, which the global graph snapshot reports.
202	        self._dependencies: dict[str, dict[str, None]] = {}
203	        self._dependents: dict[str, dict[str, None]] = {}
204	
205	    def reset(self) -> None:
206	        self._resources.clear()
207	        self._resources = []
208	        self._by_id = {}
209	        self._key_to_id = {}
210	        self._dependencies = {}
211	        self._dependents = {}
212	
213	    def list_all(self) -> list[Resource]:
214	        return list(self._resources)
215	
216	    def query(
217	        self,
218	        *,
219	        category: str | None = None,
220	        name: str | None = None,
221	        digest: str | None = None,
222	    ) -> list[Resource]:
223	        """Return matching resources in creation order.
224	
225	        ``category`` is compared case-insensitively, ``name`` is an exact
226	        string match and ``digest`` is compared against the stored lowercase
227	        form. Multiple conditions are AND-ed together.
228	        """
229	
230	        if category is None and name is None and digest is None:
231	            return list(self._resources)
232	
233	        matches: list[Resource] = []
234	        for resource in self._resources:
235	            if category is not None and resource.category != category.lower():
236	                continue
237	            if name is not None and resource.name != name:
238	                continue
239	            if digest is not None and resource.digest != digest:
240	                continue
241	            matches.append(resource)
242	        return matches
243	
244	    def get(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
245	        return self._by_id.get(resource_id)
246	
247	    def add(
248	        self, payload: object
249	    ) -> tuple[Resource | None, Resource | None]:
250	        """Validate and store a resource.
251	
252	        Returns ``(created, None)`` on success or ``(None, existing)`` when
253	        the same category, name and digest are already registered.
254	        """
255	
256	        name, category, digest, source = build_resource_fields(payload)
257	        key = (category, name, digest)
258	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
259	        if existing_id is not None:
260	            return None, self._by_id[existing_id]
261	
262	        resource = Resource(
263	            id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
264	            name=name,
265	            category=category,
266	            digest=digest,
267	            source=source,
268	        )
269	        self._resources.append(resource)
270	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
271	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
272	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = {}
273	        self._dependents[resource.id] = {}
274	        return resource, None
275	
276	    def add_remote(
277	        self,
278	        *,
279	        name: str,
280	        category: str,
281	        digest: str,
282	        source: str | None,
283	        resource_id: str | None = None,
284	    ) -> Resource:
285	        """Store a resource resolved from a remote repository.
286	
287	        The caller has already validated the fields and matched the digest
288	        against the registry, so the record is constructed directly; the
289	        same uniqueness key is enforced defensively. When ``resource_id``
290	        is given it is reused (the caller already minted it during
291	        planning); otherwise a fresh id is generated.
292	        """
293	
294	        key = (category, name, digest)
295	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
296	        if existing_id is not None:
297	            return self._by_id[existing_id]
298	
299	        resource = Resource(
300	            id=resource_id if resource_id is not None else uuid.uuid4().hex,
301	            name=name,
302	            category=category,
303	            digest=digest,
304	            source=source,
305	        )
306	        self._resources.append(resource)
307	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
308	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
309	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = {}
310	        self._dependents[resource.id] = {}
311	        return resource
312	
313	    def discard(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
314	        """Remove a resource that has no edges yet.
315	
316	        Used to roll back a resource created during an aborted operation.
317	        Only safe for resources with no dependencies or dependents.
318	        """
319	
320	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
321	        if resource is None:
322	            return
323	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
324	        self._key_to_id.pop(
325	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
326	        )
327	        self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
328	        self._dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
329	
330	    def remove(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
331	        """Remove a resource and every dependency edge touching it.
332	
333	        Returns the removed record, or ``None`` when the id is unknown.
334	        Edges the resource started and edges pointing at it disappear
335	        from both graph views; every other resource and edge is left
336	        untouched. The id is never reused by later registrations.
337	        """
338	
339	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
340	        if resource is None:
341	            return None
342	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
343	        self._key_to_id.pop(
344	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
345	        )
346	        for dependency_id in self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, ()):
347	            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
348	            if dependents is not None:
349	                dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
350	        for dependent_id in self._dependents.pop(resource_id, ()):
351	            dependencies = self._dependencies.get(dependent_id)
352	            if dependencies is not None:
353	                dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
354	        return resource
355	
356	    # --- Dependencies ------------------------------------------------------
357	
358	    def _reachable(
359	        self, start: str, graph: dict[str, dict[str, None]]
360	    ) -> set[str]:
361	        """Transitive closure of ``start`` through ``graph`` (start excluded)."""
362	
363	        seen: set[str] = set()
364	        stack = list(graph.get(start, ()))
365	        while stack:
366	            node = stack.pop()
367	            if node in seen:
368	                continue
369	            seen.add(node)
370	            stack.extend(graph.get(node, ()))
371	        return seen
372	
373	    def _registration_order(self, ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
374	        return [r.id for r in self._resources if r.id in ids]
375	
376	    def check_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
377	        """Validate an edge without mutating the graph.
378	
379	        Raises :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency``
380	        when the same-direction relation already exists, or
381	        ``dependency_cycle`` for a self loop or a relation that would
382	        introduce a cycle.
383	        """
384	
385	        if resource_id == dependency_id:
386	            raise DependencyError(
387	                "dependency_cycle", "A resource must not depend on itself."
388	            )
389	
390	        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
391	        if dependency_id in existing:
392	            raise DependencyError(
393	                "duplicate_dependency",
394	                "This dependency relation already exists.",
395	            )
396	
397	        # Adding resource_id -> dependency_id creates a cycle whenever
398	        # dependency_id can already reach resource_id.
399	        if resource_id in self._reachable(dependency_id, self._dependencies):
400	            raise DependencyError(
401	                "dependency_cycle",
402	                "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
403	            )
404	
405	    def add_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
406	        """Record that ``resource_id`` depends on ``dependency_id``.
407	
408	        Both resources must already be registered. Raises
409	        :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency`` when the
410	        same-direction relation already exists, or ``dependency_cycle`` for a
411	        self loop or a relation that would introduce a cycle; in either case
412	        the graph is left unchanged.
413	        """
414	
415	        self.check_dependency(resource_id, dependency_id)
416	        self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
417	        self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None
418	
419	    def add_dependencies(
420	        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
421	    ) -> None:
422	        """Atomically record several edges out of ``resource_id``.
423	
424	        Both the start and every depended-upon resource must already be
425	        registered (the caller checks existence); ``dependency_ids`` must
426	        come from :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields`, so it is a
427	        non-empty list of non-empty, separator-free strings in submission
428	        order. Conflict precedence is a fixed rule order, not the
429	        submission position: the whole batch is first screened for self
430	        loops, then for repeats inside the batch, then for existing
431	        same-direction edges, and finally for edges that would introduce a
432	        cycle. When several entries hit different rules at once, only the
433	        foremost rule is reported; within one rule the earliest submission
434	        position wins. A self loop or an introduced cycle raises
435	        :class:`DependencyError` with code ``dependency_cycle`` and an
436	        existing edge raises one with code ``duplicate_dependency`` (both
437	        409); an id repeated inside the batch raises
438	        :class:`ResourceValidationError` (400 ``invalid_request``), but
439	        only when no entry is a self loop, which is screened first.
440	        Every edge in the batch shares the same origin, so an accepted
441	        edge can never feed a path back to the start that did not already
442	        exist; cycle detection therefore uses the committed graph exactly
443	        like :meth:`check_dependency`. The whole batch is atomic: a
444	        failure leaves the graph exactly as it was; on success every edge is
445	        established in submission order.
446	        """
447	
448	        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
449	
450	        # Each pass is read-only; the graph is touched only once every rule
451	        # has passed, which makes the precedence independent of where in
452	        # the batch each conflict sits and guarantees all-or-nothing
453	        # behavior.
454	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
455	            if dependency_id == resource_id:
456	                raise DependencyError(
457	                    "dependency_cycle",
458	                    "A resource must not depend on itself.",
459	                )
460	
461	        seen: set[str] = set()
462	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
463	            if dependency_id in seen:
464	                raise ResourceValidationError(
465	                    "A dependency must not be listed more than once in the "
466	                    "same batch."
467	                )
468	            seen.add(dependency_id)
469	
470	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
471	            if dependency_id in existing:
472	                raise DependencyError(
473	                    "duplicate_dependency",
474	                    "This dependency relation already exists.",
475	                )
476	
477	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
478	            if resource_id in self._reachable(
479	                dependency_id, self._dependencies
480	            ):
481	                raise DependencyError(
482	                    "dependency_cycle",
483	                    "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
484	                )
485	
486	        # Every check passed; only now mutate, preserving submission order
487	        # in the ordered edge dicts.
488	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
489	            self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
490	            self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None
491	
492	    def has_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
493	        """Return whether the direct edge ``resource_id -> dependency_id`` exists."""
494	
495	        return dependency_id in self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
496	
497	    def remove_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
498	        """Remove only the direct edge from ``resource_id`` to ``dependency_id``.
499	
500	        Returns ``True`` when the edge existed and was removed, ``False``
501	        when there was no such direct edge. Neither resource record nor any
502	        other edge is touched; transitive relations that survive through
503	        other paths are left to be recomputed by the read views.
504	        """
505	
506	        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
507	        if dependencies is None or dependency_id not in dependencies:
508	            return False
509	        del dependencies[dependency_id]
510	        dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
511	        if dependents is not None:
512	            dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
513	        return True
514	
515	    def remove_dependencies(
516	        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
517	    ) -> None:
518	        """Atomically remove several direct edges out of ``resource_id``.
519	
520	        The start resource must already be registered (the caller checks
521	        existence); ``dependency_ids`` comes from
522	        :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields` with duplicate rejection on,
523	        so it is a non-empty list of distinct, non-empty, separator-free
524	        strings in submission order. Every listed direct edge must
525	        currently exist; the first submission position without such an
526	        edge raises :class:`DependencyError` with code
527	        ``dependency_not_found`` and no edge is removed, so a repeat of a
528	        failed request reports the same missing relation. Only when every
529	        edge is present are they all removed; resource records and every
530	        other edge are left untouched, and transitive relations that
531	        survive through other paths are recomputed by the read views.
532	        """
533	
534	        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
535	        if dependencies is None:
536	            raise DependencyError(
537	                "dependency_not_found",
538	                "No direct dependency relation exists from this resource "
539	                "to the requested dependency.",
540	            )
541	        # Read-only pass first: a missing entry must never leave the batch
542	        # half-deleted. The first absent position wins, in submission order.
543	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
544	            if dependency_id not in dependencies:
545	                raise DependencyError(
546	                    "dependency_not_found",
547	                    "No direct dependency relation exists from this "
548	                    "resource to the requested dependency.",
549	                )
550	
551	        # Every edge exists; remove them all after the checks.
552	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
553	            del dependencies[dependency_id]
554	            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
555	            if dependents is not None:
556	                dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
557	
558	    def list_dependencies(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
559	        """Return every reachable dependency id in registration order."""
560	
561	        return self._registration_order(
562	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependencies)
563	        )
564	
565	    def shortest_path(self, start: str, end: str) -> list[str] | None:
566	        """Return the shortest directed path from ``start`` to ``end``.
567	
568	        The path follows dependency edges in their direction (the start
569	        resource depends on the end resource) and is reported as the list
570	        of node ids, ``start`` first and ``end`` last, with no repeated
571	        nodes. ``start == end`` yields the single-node path. Returns
572	        ``None`` when ``end`` is not reachable from ``start``. Among
573	        equally short paths the one whose nodes come earliest in
574	        registration order -- compared from the second node onward -- is
575	        picked, so the answer is stable.
576	        """
577	
578	        if start == end:
579	            return [start]
580	
581	        # Hops from every node to ``end`` along the edge direction,
582	        # computed as a breadth-first walk over the reverse graph.
583	        dist: dict[str, int] = {end: 0}
584	        queue = [end]
585	        for node in queue:
586	            for predecessor in self._dependents.get(node, ()):
587	                if predecessor not in dist:
588	                    dist[predecessor] = dist[node] + 1
589	                    queue.append(predecessor)
590	        if start not in dist:
591	            return None
592	
593	        order = {
594	            resource.id: index
595	            for index, resource in enumerate(self._resources)
596	        }
597	        path = [start]
598	        current = start
599	        while current != end:
600	            remaining = dist[current]
601	            # Every candidate continues on a shortest path; taking the
602	            # earliest-registered one at each step yields the stable pick.
603	            current = min(
604	                (
605	                    successor
606	                    for successor in self._dependencies.get(current, ())
607	                    if dist.get(successor) == remaining - 1
608	                ),
609	                key=lambda node: order[node],
610	            )
611	            path.append(current)
612	        return path
613	
614	    def all_shortest_paths(
615	        self, start: str, end: str
616	    ) -> list[list[str]] | None:
617	        """Return every shortest directed path from ``start`` to ``end``.
618	
619	        Each path follows dependency edges in their direction (the start
620	        resource depends on the end resource) and is reported as the list
621	        of node ids, ``start`` first and ``end`` last, with no repeated
622	        nodes. ``start == end`` yields the single single-node path.
623	        Returns ``None`` when ``end`` is not reachable from ``start``.
624	        The paths are ordered stably: by the second node's registration
625	        order first, then by each subsequent node's registration order.
626	        """
627	
628	        if start == end:
629	            return [[start]]
630	
631	        # Hops from every node to ``end`` along the edge direction,
632	        # computed as a breadth-first walk over the reverse graph.
633	        dist: dict[str, int] = {end: 0}
634	        queue = [end]
635	        for node in queue:
636	            for predecessor in self._dependents.get(node, ()):
637	                if predecessor not in dist:
638	                    dist[predecessor] = dist[node] + 1
639	                    queue.append(predecessor)
640	        if start not in dist:
641	            return None
642	
643	        # Enumerate every shortest path: from each node only the successors
644	        # exactly one hop closer to ``end`` can continue a shortest path.
645	        # The graph is a DAG, so the walk always terminates.
646	        paths: list[list[str]] = []
647	        stack: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = [(start, [start])]
648	        while stack:
649	            node, path = stack.pop()
650	            if node == end:
651	                paths.append(path)
652	                continue
653	            remaining = dist[node]
654	            for successor in self._dependencies.get(node, ()):
